facts.statement: Rauisuchus, meaning "Wilhelm Rau's crocodile", is an extinct genus of archosaurs that lived in Brazil during the Late Triassic period between 235 and 228 million years ago.
facts.quote: Rauisuchus (meaning "Wilhelm Rau's crocodile") is a genus of extinct archosaurs which lived in what is now the Geopark of Paleorrota (Santa María Formation), Brazil, during the Late Triassic period (235–228 million years ago).

facts.statement: Dr. Wilhelm Rau discovered Rauisuchus remains near the road from Santa Maria to San Jose in 1928 or 1929 while working under Friedrich von Huene.
facts.quote: In 1928 or 1929, near the road from Santa Maria to San Jose, Dr. Wilhelm Rau, a German fossil collector working under Friedrich von Huene, discovered the remains of a rauisuchid crocodile.

facts.statement: The discovery site, known as Zahnsanga, was located 20 to 30 meters from the road and was likely a ravine or escarpment.
facts.quote: He made the discovery some 20 - 30 m from the road at a site known as the Zahnsanga, which was likely a ravine or escarpment parallel to the road.

facts.statement: Krebs described the tarsus of R. tiradentes in 1973, and the lectotype was assigned in 1976.
facts.quote: Krebs (1973) described the tarsus of R. tiradentes and the lectotype was assigned in 1976

facts.statement: Lautenschlager and Rauhut removed remains from Locality 15 ('Find 1020') from the genus in 2014 because they could not be diagnostically assigned to Rauisuchus.
facts.quote: Lautenschlager & Rauhut (2014) found that the remains from Locality 15 ('Find 1020') could not be diagnostically assigned to Rauisuchus, and so were removed from the genus.

facts.statement: Rauisuchus is distinguished by a knob-like thickening on the premaxilla, short ventrally keeled cervical vertebrae, and elongated caudals with specific neural spines and laminae.
facts.quote: Rauisuchus is distinguished from other members of the Rauisuchidae on the basis of a knob-like thickening on the base of the posterior process of the premaxilla, short, ventrally keeled cervicals, lacking postzygodiapophyseal laminae, and elongated caudals with an accessory neural spine and a postspinal lamina.

facts.statement: Rauisuchus belongs to the Rauisuchidae, a group of land-dwelling crocodile relatives, though it was initially assigned to the Theriodontia in 1936.
facts.quote: Rauisuchus belonged to a group of land-dwelling relatives to crocodiles known as the Rauisuchidae, although it was initially assigned to the Theriodontia in 1936.

facts.statement: Rauisuchus is placed as the sister taxon to Tikisuchus and Yarasuchus, forming a clade with them.
facts.quote: It was placed as the sister taxon to Tikisuchus and Yarasuchus, forming a clade with the two.

facts.statement: Rauisuchids were top predators that ate other reptiles and possibly hunted early dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Rauisuchids were among the top predators of their day, eating other reptiles for food and maybe hunting early dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Rauisuchus lived in what is now the Paleorrota Geopark in Brazil during the middle Triassic period, between 240 and 230 million years ago.
facts.quote: izquierda|miniaturadeimagen Rauisuchus es un género extinto de arcosaurio que vivió en lo que ahora es el Geoparque de Paleorrota en Brasil, durante mediados del período Triásico (hace entre 240-230 millones de años).

facts.statement: The time range for Rauisuchus spans from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Friedrich von Huene sent the Rauisuchus tiradentes material back to Germany alongside other fossils, including the holotype of Prestosuchus chiniquensis.
rejected.quote: von Huene then sent the R. tiradentes material back to Germany alongside other fossils, including the holotype of Prestosuchus chiniquensis.
